run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-14T20:24:55Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is explained by a short, real 5xx burst at the frontend-proxy edge that follows the frontend's failed gRPC calls to cart. At 2026-11-14T20:27:25Z the cart Deployment was rolled out again (pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-14T20:27:25Z, same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart); the replacement pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz was reported Ready at 20:27:28Z, one second after its container started, although the cart container has no readiness/startup probe and the cart process logged its ASP.NET startup line only at 20:27:50.911Z. The old cart pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 was stopped at 20:27:28Z, so for roughly 20 s the cart Service (a single endpoint) had no process able to serve. frontend-proxy access logs show the first 500 at 20:27:29.371Z on POST /api/cart, with GET /api/cart and POST /api/checkout failing through 20:27:49.987Z; frontend's own span counters moved in the same scrape interval (+70 POST server errors, +52 grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem client errors, also GetCart and tcp.connect errors), and cart's span-metric instance rolled over at the same scrape. Ingress ERROR span counts at frontend-proxy rose from 0-6 per 5 min to 105.6-108.9 per 5 min for the windows ending 20:29:00-20:33:00 and were back to 5.6 by 20:34:00; about 100 error spans against about 10,000-10,400 ingress spans per 15 min is roughly 1%, the same order as the 1.1% in the alert. Affected, with their own failure evidence tied to this cause: frontend-proxy and frontend. Changed during the window: the cart Deployment rollout (named as the change; its trigger is unknown) and, separately, fraud-detection's OOMKilled restart at 20:32:56Z, which shows no connection to the error signal. Not cleared: checkout, whose frontend client spans failed while checkout's own spans carry no ERROR status. The alert's recorded start (20:24:55Z) is about 2.5 minutes before the first observed 500 and the alerting rule could not be read, so the exact evaluation window and threshold are unverified.

claims.text: frontend-proxy ingress ERROR spans (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}) increased by 105.6-108.9 per 5-minute window for the windows ending 20:29:00, 20:30:00, 20:31:00, 20:32:00 and 20:33:00, versus 0-6 per 5 minutes for the windows ending 20:12:00-20:28:00, and fell to 5.6 for the window ending 20:34:00.

The raw ingress ERROR counter for frontend-proxy was 596 at the 20:28:25 scrape and 689 at the 20:28:55 scrape (+93 in one scrape interval), then stayed essentially flat (692 by 20:29:55, 698 by 20:43:55).

In the 15-minute windows ending 20:24:55-20:44:55, frontend-proxy span_name="ingress" STATUS_CODE_ERROR increases were 34.6, 37.2, 38.5, 7.2, 103.4, 103.4, 106.5 and 6.3, while the same windows' ingress STATUS_CODE_UNSET increases were about 2,975-10,412, and span_name="router frontend egress" ERROR increases were 0 except 96.2/96.2/96.2 in the three windows containing the burst.

frontend-proxy access logs show the first HTTP 500 of the window at 2026-11-14T20:27:29.371559Z ("POST /api/cart HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream), followed by 500s on POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart and POST /api/checkout; 35 500-response lines are logged in that pod between 20:27:29 and 20:27:39.

500 responses at frontend-proxy on POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart and POST /api/checkout continue through 20:27:49.987242Z (for example "POST /api/cart HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream at 20:27:49.654266Z and "GET /api/cart HTTP/1.1" 500 at 20:27:49.868925Z).
At 20:35:16-20:35:19Z the same frontend-proxy pod logs 200 responses for POST /api/cart, GET /api/cart, GET /api/data and GET /api/products/*, i.e. the edge error burst had ended.

frontend's own error span counters jumped in exactly the same scrape interval: span_name="POST" status ERROR went 71 -> 141 (+70) and client span grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem status ERROR went 11 -> 63 (+52) between the 20:28:25 and 20:28:55 samples, and both counters show no further increase through 20:43:30.

frontend error spans are confined to the burst: in 4-minute buckets from 19:58 to 20:46, span_name POST, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, executing api route (pages) /api/cart, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, GET, GET /api/cart and tcp.connect are non-zero only at the 20:29:55 and 20:31:55 evaluation points and zero before and after.

frontend's POST status ERROR counter was already 71 and flat for every sample from 19:54:00 to 20:22:00, so the earlier accumulated errors are distinct from the 20:28 burst and the counter did not increase during that earlier period.

cart's span-metric series for POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem shows two instances: exported_instance aca18cfb-2104-4fea-af05-8927cccd126c stops growing at 3279 from the 20:28:55 sample onward, while exported_instance 0cc5b36b-afc1-4767-84c2-a7bcc30f2904 first appears at the 20:28:55 sample with 31 and grows to 1098 by 20:43:55.

Kubernetes events for the cart Deployment: ScalingReplicaSet "Scaled up replica set cart-84889c965d from 0 to 1" and SuccessfulCreate of pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz at 20:27:25Z; Scheduled 20:27:25Z; "Started container cart" 20:27:27Z; Killing "Stopping container cart" for pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 and SuccessfulDelete of that pod at 20:27:28Z; "Scaled down replica set cart-755465879b from 1 to 0" at 20:27:28Z.

The new cart ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d carries the pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt="2026-11-14T20:27:25Z" and image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-cart, the same image as the previous ReplicaSet cart-755465879b (created 19:56:15Z); the cart Deployment is at generation 2 and deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 2.

The cart Deployment runs 1 replica with strategy RollingUpdate maxSurge 25% / maxUnavailable 25%, and its Progressing condition ("ReplicaSet cart-84889c965d has successfully progressed") has lastUpdateTime 2026-11-14T20:27:28Z.

New cart pod cart-84889c965d-tkxdz: container cart startedAt 20:27:27Z, container ready=true, and the pod's Ready and ContainersReady conditions have lastTransitionTime 2026-11-14T20:27:28Z, one second after the container started.

The cart container spec has readinessProbe: null, livenessProbe: null and startupProbe: null, exposes containerPort 8080 (name service), and has limits cpu 45m / memory 165Mi and requests cpu 15m / memory 55Mi.

The cart container logged its ASP.NET startup line ("Overriding HTTP_PORTS '{http}' and HTTPS_PORTS '{https}'. Binding to values defined by URLS instead '{urls}'.") at 2026-11-14T20:27:50.9111852Z, about 23 seconds after the container started at 20:27:27Z.
All 21 otel-demo pods are Running and Ready, cart-84889c965d-tkxdz has container cart restartCount 0 with an empty lastState, and the cart Service currently has the single endpoint 100.96.1.157:8080.

fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-v48vh has restartCount 1 with last termination reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-14T20:32:55Z and restarted at 20:32:56Z; its events show container Created and Started at 20:32:56Z.

In the 22-minute ERROR aggregate ending 20:46:00, ERROR-status series were returned for frontend, frontend-proxy, ad (flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 1.03), fraud-detection (flagd EventStream 1.03) and recommendation (/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream 2.06); cart and checkout series were returned with value 0 (for example checkout oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 0); no ERROR series was returned for currency, email, shipping, product-catalog, quote, image-provider, kafka or load-generator.

The newest traces Jaeger returned for frontend within 19:24:55-20:24:55 have start_us 1794687200395000-1794687201254000 (20:13:20.395-20:13:20.254Z), and every span in that returned sample carries http.status_code 200 or rpc.grpc.status_code 0.

Primary cause: the cart Deployment rollout restart at 2026-11-14T20:27:25Z removed the only serving cart pod at 20:27:28Z while the replacement pod was already marked Ready at 20:27:28Z (it has no readiness or startup probe) but its process only began serving at 20:27:50.9Z. For about 20 seconds the cart Service endpoint could not serve gRPC, so frontend's CartService and tcp.connect calls failed and frontend returned 500 on /api/cart and /api/checkout, which frontend-proxy surfaced as ingress and router-egress 5xx; roughly 100 error spans against roughly 10,000 ingress spans per 15 minutes is about 1%, the same order as the 1.1% error rate in the alert.

Contributing configuration, not proven as an independent cause: because cart has a single replica and no readiness or startup probe, a rolling restart driven by restartedAt on a 1-replica Deployment (maxSurge 25% / maxUnavailable 25%) could not keep a serving endpoint through the swap, so frontend and frontend-proxy had to turn cart connection failures into 5xx.

The error signal is transient and no longer produced: frontend's POST and grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem error counters show no increase after the 20:28:55 sample, and frontend-proxy logs 200 responses for /api/cart and /api/checkout from 20:35:16Z onward.

The cart pod shows no crash or resource kill of its own: cart-84889c965d-tkxdz has restartCount 0 and an empty lastState, and its replacement is recorded as a controller rollout (SuccessfulCreate cart-84889c965d / SuccessfulDelete cart-755465879b-rh5r4) rather than an Evicted or OOMKilled termination.

Rejected: the fraud-detection OOMKilled restart (exit 137 at 20:32:55Z, restarted 20:32:56Z) caused the frontend-proxy error rate. The 5xx burst precedes it (first observed 500 at 20:27:29.371Z), frontend's error counters show no increment after the 20:28:55 sample, the 5-minute ingress error increase had already dropped to 5.6 by the 20:34:00 evaluation, and frontend-proxy was serving 200s at 20:35.

Rejected: cart was OOMKilled or evicted, i.e. the cart pod failed on its own. There is no OOMKilled termination or Evicted event for cart, the new cart container has restartCount 0 and an empty lastState, and the pod transition is documented by the Deployment's own SuccessfulCreate/SuccessfulDelete events.

Add a readinessProbe (and startupProbe) on the cart container's port 8080 so that pod Ready reflects the process actually serving, and for single-replica deployments use maxUnavailable: 0 with surge or run more than one cart replica, so a restart cannot remove the only serving endpoint.

Review the RequestErrorRate rule definition and the cart rollout audit trail together: confirm the rule's window and threshold (the rule could not be read in this Run) and establish who or what issued the kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-14T20:27:25Z restart, then decide whether such restarts should be scheduled away from single-replica dependencies.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule could not be inspected: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data both for rule_name=RequestErrorRate and for type=alert, so the rule's expression, window and threshold (and therefore the exact 0.01111111111111111 figure) are unknown; the alert's recorded start 20:24:55Z also precedes the first observed 500 (20:27:29.371Z) by about 2.5 minutes and that discrepancy is unexplained.

change_history is not an integrated source in this Run, so who or what triggered the cart rollout restart (kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-14T20:27:25Z) is unknown, and the old cart pod cart-755465879b-rh5r4 no longer exists, so its image_id and last container state cannot be compared with the new pod.

Jaeger holds no traces after about 20:13:21Z: traces_search for frontend and for frontend-proxy in later windows, traces_search_by_tags for frontend and frontend-proxy with error=true in 20:24:55-20:46:20, and traces_search for cart in 20:15:00-20:46:20 all returned no_data, so the 20:27 burst could not be inspected as traces and the frontend's gRPC status codes or error messages for the failed cart calls were not observed.

The frontend container produced no log lines in 19:24:55-20:46:20 (0 bytes read) so there is no application-level error text from frontend; the cart container's logs contain no error/fail lines; and fraud-detection's previous-container (pre-OOM) log stream was unavailable.

The frontend-proxy log read for 19:24:55 onward hit the 4 MiB read limit and only reached 20:25:45.8Z, so frontend-proxy lines after that cut in that query are unread (they were re-read successfully in narrower windows).

Span-metric series for frontend-proxy and frontend have no samples before 20:06:25-20:06:30 and the first ingress ERROR sample is already 557, so the earlier error accumulation and the small residual rate (~2-6 ingress error spans per 5 min before the burst) could not be attributed or bounded; also traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket was never broken down by service, so no latency trend is asserted and no latency baseline was established.

The rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count metric used to look for gRPC status codes does not exist in this source (label-value, all-labels and range queries returned no_data), so per-call gRPC status labels could not be checked; only span status_code labels were available.

checkout is not cleared: frontend's client spans to grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder recorded errors in the burst while checkout's own server spans carry no ERROR status, and checkout's finer-grained internal error evidence was not available.

The frontend-proxy ingress ERROR view for 22 minutes was returned at a single evaluation point, so the breakdown of errors by individual HTTP path and response code at frontend-proxy rests only on the sampled access-log lines shown, not on a complete count.
next_steps: Fetch the RequestErrorRate rule (and its Alertmanager route/grouping) from the monitoring configuration to confirm its window, threshold and why StartsAt is 20:24:55Z.
Check the Kubernetes/CI audit log around 2026-11-14T20:27:25Z for the actor and reason behind the cart Deployment restart (rollout restart).

Add readinessProbe/startupProbe on cart port 8080 and set the cart Deployment to maxUnavailable: 0 with surge (or more than one replica), then repeat a restart test in a non-production namespace to confirm no 5xx at frontend-proxy.

If this alert is meant to be low-noise, consider a short 'for:' duration or an error-rate threshold above this roughly 1% transient, since the observed 5xx burst was self-healing within about 20 seconds.
